vBRIEFInfo.description: Make package-manager (npm/pnpm) network access explicit and security-scoped: read-only/session/ritual flows perform no registry access; doctor separates offline from network tiers; network-enabled checks are explicit and disclosed (#2182).

plan.title: Make package-manager network access explicit and security-scoped

narratives.Description: Directive runs against arbitrary repos incl. private monorepos. Session/ritual/doctor/read-only flows must not silently invoke npm/pnpm commands that can contact registries (disclosing package names/scopes/graph shape, tripping sandbox network approval, or creating confusing prompts). Registry traffic itself is sensitive. Package-manager network access must be opt-in, offline-by-default where possible, and disclosed before it runs.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Audit session:start, the session-start ritual, doctor, and read-only flows for any npm/pnpm invocation that can reach a registry (identify the exact call sites in scripts/doctor.py or the TS doctor, session-ritual, verify:tools, and taskfiles). 2. Ensure read-only/session/ritual flows perform NO package-manager network access — use offline/frozen modes (e.g. --offline / --prefer-offline / --frozen-lockfile / npm --offline) or skip entirely. 3. Split doctor into an offline tier (default, no registry) and an explicit network/package-manager tier gated behind a flag/command; the network tier discloses which tool + registry class it may contact BEFORE running. 4. Any command that may contact npm/pnpm registries is explicit in name, output, and approval prompt. 5. Tests: a fixture repo with a private-scope registry config; assert session:start and read-only flows invoke NO npm/pnpm (inject/stub the package-manager seam and assert it is not called with network). 6. Docs: state that package-manager network access is sensitive and opt-in. IMPORTANT: put any agent-facing guidance in a CONTENT DOC (e.g. content/tools/ or content/scm/), NOT in AGENTS.md or content/templates/agents-entry.md (a parallel reduction lane owns those files). Run task check GREEN; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator running directive against a private monorepo, I want session/health/read-only flows to never silently hit npm/pnpm registries, so my package scopes and dependency graph aren't disclosed and I don't get confusing network-approval prompts.

items.title: Read-only/session/ritual flows do no pkg-manager network access

narrative.Acceptance: task session:start and read-only flows perform no npm/pnpm registry access (verified by a stubbed seam asserting no network invocation).

items.title: Doctor offline tier vs network tier

narrative.Acceptance: task doctor runs an offline tier by default without contacting registries; network-enabled dependency checks require an explicit command/flag and disclose the tool + registry class first.
Any command that may contact npm/pnpm registries is explicit in name/output/approval prompt; offline/frozen modes used where possible.
Tests cover a repo with private scope registry config and verify session/read-only flows do not invoke npm/pnpm with network.
